description:
Files:
- lib/zaq/engine/channel_config.ex
- lib/zaq/connector_config/settings.ex
- config/config.ex
- config/runtime.exs
- proposed Channels linked-device configuration module

Functional specifications:
Register WhatsApp through current config owner; allow URL/token-free setup. Derive stable string profile from exact channel_config_id and use the same resolver everywhere. No arbitrary profile UI overrides initially; any compatibility overrides require uniqueness and consistent ingress/egress resolution. Translate allowlisted JSON string keys safely. Enforce sync_history=false and sync_full_history=false after merging options. Configure the custom Amarula storage adapter through the bridge; omit storage_root. Resolve the exact credential association through existing ZAQ Credentials/Connect boundaries. No filesystem storage requirement. Define one runtime owner per connector across nodes; default Amarula registry uniqueness is node-local.
Architecture refinement: Shared configuration contract carries connector/credential identity and delegates provider-specific profile/settings resolution. Amarula sync flags remain in WhatsApp binding.
Assert exact runtime options reach jido_chat_whatsapp: connector-derived profile, custom storage association, sync_history=false, sync_full_history=false, no storage_root override.

Tests before implementation:
- Two same-provider configs yield distinct stable profiles
- Persisted string keys cannot enable sync
- Reload/reconnect keeps profile
- Malformed settings and conflicting override fail
- Property test profile and configuration isolation
- Runtime options preserve custom storage and omit storage_root
- Connector-to-credential association cannot cross profiles
- Exercise shared contract with a minimal fake second provider; keep WhatsApp-specific expectations in provider contract tests

Branches validated:
- create
- edit
- reload
- disabled
- duplicate profile
- storage failure

Documentation:
- docs/services/channels.md
- docs/services/system-config.md
- operator credential-backed session persistence
- module contracts

Action reuse assessment:
Extend Engine ChannelConfig and ConnectorConfig.Settings CRUD. Runtime option/profile translation is local transport logic. Exact config in, validated options or error out; no connection side effects. Existing BO persistence boundary stays authoritative; no new tool. Inspect and reuse existing device-connection behavior before adding shared modules; document any missing contract as a prerequisite. No duplicate provider-specific credential store or pairing framework.

Validation:
Follow docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md validation lifecycle; tests before implementation, focused checks per issue, final gate before approval. No live account connection or send without scoped authorization.

Mocking:
External Amarula transport only; use real internal boundaries and isolated DB/process/storage fixtures; inject config and clock without global mutation.

Policy:
Recheck module responsibilities, docs/services/channels.md, Action reuse, system-config and testing guidance before coding. BO calls use explicit NodeRouter Events; nil actor never grants permission.

comments.text: Completed and pushed 2293cdea7. Shared pure config/provider contract, stable profile per persisted connector, explicit trusted storage binding, WhatsApp registration and token/URL-free persistence via existing placeholders. WhatsApp history flags forced false; settings cannot override profile/storage. Tests include actual upstream listener-spec pass-through, two database configs, generic second-provider stub and profile-isolation property. mix q and 57 tests/1 property passed. Lifecycle wiring and credential association remain in dependent issues. Discovered upstream/zaq-p8t/device-code-sign-in: its HTTP polling/token-exchange behavior is OAuth-specific, unsuitable for direct Amarula socket pairing; reuse credential infrastructure rather than that protocol interface.
